notes: George Washington, Stars and Stripes (sheet 187). Cards read from the images of the tournament save on 2026-11-13 and compared with unmatched-memory's transcription: no differences (docs/heroes/george-washington.md).

Additive engine pieces: none in the DSL. ESPIONAGE uses the existing counters and the `attacked` and `after_attack` events; the code is three plugins (`sparring/effects/plugins_washington.py`), the AI (`sparring/ai_washington.py`) and the human's side of the declaration at Reveal (`sparring/session_espionage.py`).
Rules decisions taken without an official ruling are listed in docs/heroes/george-washington.md, 'Pending Ivan'.

ability.text:
ESPIONAGE
You start with 4 ruse tokens.
When you attack, you may use a ruse token, placing it next to the card.
Before your opponent chooses whether or not to defend, they may discard 1 random card to remove the ruse token.
ability.notes: Two counters. `ruse_tokens` is the supply (4 at the start; Misinformation and Sympathetic Stain give one back, never above 4). `ruse` is 1 while a ruse token lies next to the card of the attack in progress: the [RUSE] part of a card (printed after the ruse-triangle icon) reads it with the condition `counter ruse`, which is the reading 'applies only if the ruse token is still on the card' (Pending Ivan 1). Triggers, all on events the interpreter already has: `espionage` (an enemy fighter is attacked: you attack) asks the attacker whether to spend a token (plugin `washington:use_ruse`; only a card that carries a ruse effect, tag `ruse`, is worth the question); `espionage_remove` asks the OPPONENT, before they choose their defense, whether to discard 1 random card to remove the token (plugin `washington:offer_removal`: the yes/no goes to the opponent, who pays the price of Incinerate's kind, a card of their hand, at random); `espionage_clear` takes the token off when the combat is over. A token the opponent removes is gone, it does not return to the supply (Pending Ivan 3).

cards.title: Lead Astray
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: Move a fighter in the combat up to 2 spaces.
cards.notes: Attack 5 / boost 2, Washington only. Skirmish's move (Bigfoot, Tomoe Gozen, Golden Bat, Eredin) without the 'if you won' condition: the owner picks which of the two fighters and where.

cards.title: Agent 711
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: [RUSE] If you won the combat, deal 7 damage to the opposing fighter.
cards.notes: Attack 4 / boost 3, Washington only. [RUSE] is read as 'only while the ruse token is still on the card' (the counter `ruse`; docs/heroes/george-washington.md, Pending Ivan 1). Effect damage, so the immune_to_effect_damage statuses stop it.

cards.title: Allies Everywhere
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: Gain 1 free action to attack. [RUSE] Washington recovers 3 health.
cards.notes: Attack 1 / boost 3, Washington only. The free action is attack-only (only: attack, Ivan 2026-11-13). The heal reaches the hero, not the fighter that played the card.

cards.title: Circumvent
cards.text: DURING COMBAT: [RUSE] Ignore the value of your opponent's card.
cards.notes: Attack 3 / boost 2, any fighter. The 'ignore the value' of Bullseye and Doctor Strange (set_value ignore), behind the ruse.

cards.title: Sabotage
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: [RUSE] If you won the combat, your opponent discards 2 random cards.
cards.notes: Attack 3 / boost 3, any fighter. `pick: random` on the rival's hand looks at nothing (docs/effects-dsl.md section 6).

cards.title: Misinformation
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: If you won the combat, regain a ruse token.
cards.notes: Versatile 4 / boost 2, any fighter. The counter is clipped at 4: a fifth token is not kept.

cards.title: Make A Stand
cards.text: DURING COMBAT: If your fighter started this turn in their current space, this card's value becomes 5.
cards.notes: Versatile 3 / boost 1, any fighter. Plugin test `washington:started_here`: the fighter's current space is the one it had at the start of the turn (it may leave and come back; Ivan 2026-11-13). A fighter with no start-of-turn space (a Spy placed this turn) does not count.

cards.title: Feint
cards.text: IMMEDIATELY: Cancel all effects on your opponent's card.
cards.notes: Versatile 2 / boost 3, any fighter. The shared Feint (source id 2).

cards.title: Recruit To The Ring
cards.text: AFTER COMBAT: Return a defeated Spy to a space adjacent to Washington. If you won the combat, return that Spy to any space instead.
cards.notes: Versatile 2 / boost 1, any fighter. A returned Spy comes back with 1 health (they have no more). With no free space next to Washington the revive finds nowhere to put it and does nothing.

cards.title: Network Of Spies
cards.text: DURING COMBAT: Add +1 to this card's value for each other friendly fighter in Washington's zone.
cards.notes: Versatile 2 / boost 2, Washington only. `other` leaves out the fighter that plays the card, Washington himself.

cards.title: Undercover Agent
cards.text: DURING COMBAT: Washington may swap spaces with an adjacent Spy. If he does, that Spy is now the defender.
cards.notes: Defense 1 / boost 2, Washington only. Eredin's Portal Defense mechanism (the swapped Spy takes Washington's place in the combat), but in DURING and optional.

cards.title: Sympathetic Stain
cards.text: Choose an opponent and look at their hand. If a Spy is adjacent to one of their fighters, choose a card for them to discard and regain a ruse token.
cards.notes: Scheme, boost 3, played by a Spy (band SPY). The look is always made; the discard and the token need a living Spy next to any of their fighters when the card resolves. 'Choose an opponent': there is only one.

cards.title: Gather Information
cards.text: Draw 3 cards. Move each of your fighters up to 3 spaces. They may move through opposing fighters.
cards.notes: Scheme, boost 2, Washington only. Eredin's Close For The Kill with one more card.

plugins.why: ESPIONAGE: the attacker's yes/no must carry the attack card (the bot weighs the ruse of THAT card) and the question is skipped for a card with no ruse effect; an `optional` op cannot see the attack of the event.

ESPIONAGE: the opponent's yes/no must say who is attacked (the bot weighs the ruse of the attack against THAT fighter) and its price is a random card of their own hand, paid as a voluntary discard; an `optional` with a `cost` cannot carry the target.

Make A Stand: 'started this turn in their current space' compares the current space with the one recorded at the start of the turn; no condition says 'is where it started' (moved_this_turn is false for a fighter with no recorded start).
Undercover Agent: after the swap, the Spy takes Washington's place as the defender IN the running combat (Eredin's Portal Defense, Houdini's Smoke And Mirrors), which no op can do.

hidden_info.bot_rule: `pick: random`: nothing is read. Against the human the engine draws the positions and the human discards those; against the bot the engine draws them and the table follows.
hidden_info.human_plays_it: the bot says the positions of the cards to discard, counted from the left, as for Backhand.

hidden_info.what: look at the rival's hand and choose a card for them to discard.
hidden_info.bot_rule: the bot sees the human's hand through `look_hand` (the one op that shows it) and discards the most valuable card it saw; the discard and the token only happen with a Spy next to one of their fighters.
hidden_info.human_plays_it: the bot shows its hand in the row and the human pings the card (the usual look-and-discard route).

hidden_info.what: the ruse token lies next to a face-down attack card.
hidden_info.bot_rule: the bot's decision to remove the token (discard a random card) uses public information only: the unseen cards of Washington's deck that carry a ruse effect, never the card played.
hidden_info.human_plays_it: the human says at Reveal whether the token is on the attack; the bot answers before it chooses its defense.

open_questions: [RUSE] read as 'applies only if the ruse token is still on the card' (an inference from the transcription).
A ruse token the opponent removes is spent, not returned to Washington's supply.
Any fighter of Washington's may use a ruse token ('when you attack': you), a Spy included.
